finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[EVT-1] Synchronous email sends block API route
File: src/app/api/send/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: The POST handler constructs a nodemailer transporter and calls transporter.sendMail() inline with no queue, no idempotency key, and no background retry/DLQ. This makes each HTTP request wait on external SMTP calls.
Impact: A 10x spike in order-confirmation calls will exhaust serverless/concurrency slots, cause high latency/timeouts, trigger client/provider retries and likely duplicate emails or failed deliveries.  
Fix: Immediately offload email sends to a durable background queue/worker or use transactional outbox + worker (or a managed email service/webhook) and add idempotency keys.

[EVT-2] WhatsApp sends performed synchronously without throttling
File: src/app/api/whatsapp/route.ts (L1-L300)
Evidence: The POST handler issues a direct fetch to the WhatsApp Business API and returns its result synchronously with no queuing, rate-limiting, deduplication, or DLQ. The client lib (src/lib/whatsapp.ts) calls this endpoint directly.
Impact: A 10x spike will quickly hit WhatsApp rate limits and produce high outbound latency/timeouts, causing failed requests, duplicate notifications from retries, and potential provider blocking.  
Fix: Introduce an async queue with rate-limit/backoff and idempotency keys; throttle producers and push retries to a DLQ for manual inspection.

[EVT-3] Large uploads buffered in-route (OOM/backlog risk)
File: src/app/api/upload/route.ts (L1-L260)
Evidence: The route reads the uploaded File into memory via file.arrayBuffer() -> Buffer and then uploads to R2, allowing videos up to 500MB and no streaming or concurrency caps.  
Impact: A 10x concurrent-upload spike (or several large files) will exhaust memory, crash or severely degrade server processes, and create huge request backlogs and failed client uploads.  
Fix: Replace in-route buffering with direct client-to-R2 uploads (presigned URLs) or streaming uploads, enforce strict per-request size and concurrency limits, and offload processing to background workers.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[EVT-4] Heavy CSV export done synchronously in request
File: src/app/api/admin/orders/export/route.ts (L1-L400)
Evidence: The POST handler loads many orders, iterates all orderItems, builds entire CSV in memory and returns it directly (no streaming, no job offload).  
Impact: Repeated/parallel exports (10x) will spike DB CPU and memory, slow other requests, and increase latency for user-facing endpoints.  
Fix: Offload large exports to background jobs that write CSV to object storage and return a presigned download link, or stream paginated results to the response.

[EVT-5] No dead-letter, retry, or idempotency patterns repository-wide
File: package.json / prisma/schema.prisma (repo context)
Evidence: package.json contains no queue/workflow libraries (Bull/BullMQ/Temporal/Inngest/etc.) and prisma schema has no ProcessedEvent/Outbox table or unique processed-event id fields.  
Impact: Under a 10x spike external failures and transient errors will cause immediate failures or client retry storms with no durable retry/DLQ path and high risk of duplicate side effects.  
Fix: Introduce a durable queue or outbox pattern, persist event IDs with unique constraints, and add DLQ/exhausted-retry alerts.

[EVT-6] N+1 DB lookups when assembling abandoned carts
File: src/app/api/admin/abandoned-carts/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: The GET handler maps over partial checkouts and — inside Promise.all — runs prisma.findUnique for cart and then per-item prisma.findUnique for product, producing many sequential DB queries per request.  
Impact: A 10x spike (or many carts) causes DB connection/CPU pressure, long response times, and possible timeouts/backpressure on the app tier.  
Fix: Batch fetch related cart and product data with joined/IN queries (single findMany with includes) and paginate results to limit per-request load.

--- INFO ---

[EVT-7] No queue library detected in dependencies
File: package.json (repo context)
Evidence: Dependencies list contains svix, nodemailer, etc., but no queue/workflow libraries (Bull, BullMQ, Inngest, Temporal, SQS SDK wrappers), indicating synchronous in-route side effects.
